issue.title: Render eighth-level fluid tops and partial step faces
issue.body:
## Background

After #2517 fluid tops render as flat whole-z steps, #2520 supplies exact
signed eighth-z surfaces, and #2525 supplies eight owner-approved level
masks. This issue integrates those prerequisites in one implementation PR:
every fluid top uses its exact height and matching mask, and visible sides
terminate at the neighbouring fluid or terrain surface.

Verified against `master` `5b677136fdac` (2026-09-10), before those
prerequisites:

- `src/World/Render/TileQuads.hs` places fluid tops from integer heights.
  `src/World/Render/SideDecoQuads.hs` emits whole-z side stacks, excludes
  Ocean, and conservatively omits edges against unloaded neighbours.
- `src/World/Render/Quads.hs` uses integer slice/depth visibility, suppresses
  Lake/Ocean tops under ice, and renders ice at its independent `icSurface`.
  `src/World/Fluid/Ice.hs` derives a base from terrain and fluid, puts drape
  ice one z above it, and caps basin thickness at 20 z.
- Structural masks travel through startup preload, world-view loading,
  initial world binding, Lua texture-name parsing, and the world texture
  command. Late structural rebinding invalidates cached quads.
- The shader uses face-map alpha for silhouette and RGB for directional
  lighting (`src/Engine/Graphics/Vulkan/ShaderCode.hs`). The #2525 masks
  already include side pixels: their top diamond stays unchanged and their
  side extrusion is `2 * level` pixels.

The prerequisites must land before implementation. Their absence from the
snapshot above does not expand this issue into state migration or asset
creation.

## Requirements

1. Load and bind all eight approved masks through the complete existing
   route: `scripts/startup_loader.lua`,
   `worldView.ensureStructuralTextures`, initial binding in
   `scripts/world_manager.lua`, `worldView.rebindStructural`,
   `parseTextureType` in `src/Engine/Scripting/Lua/Material.hs`,
   `World.Texture.Types`, `World.Render.Textures.Types`, and
   `handleWorldSetTextureCommand`. Each level resolves to its documented
   mask handle on both initial binding and late rebinding. Preserve quad,
   zoom, and background cache invalidation so late loads become visible
   without camera movement. `tools/check_texture_paths.py` must see every
   asset reference.
2. River, Lake, Lava, and Ocean select masks using the exact `topFillLevel`
   helper from #2520: levels 1..8, with every exact multiple mapped to 8.
   Never select by float rounding. Place the flat top at the exact surface
   height, converting to floating point only at the final rendering
   boundary. Neighbouring heights do not slope the top.
3. For each camera-visible edge, compare exact owning and neighbouring
   fluid planes; a dry neighbour contributes its terrain surface. Full-z
   and partial side segments must cover exactly the exposed interval,
   without gaps or duplicate coverage. This contract applies to the
   combined silhouette of the selected top mask and separate side
   geometry: account for side pixels already present in the mask. Unequal
   left/right neighbour heights must terminate independently. Equal or
   higher neighbours produce no exposed side, including an enclosed
   equal-height cell. An unloaded neighbour produces no invented edge.
   Preserve the approved mask files; geometry integration owns any
   clipping or coverage coordination needed to meet this contract.
4. Ocean uses the same level-selection and side-geometry path as the other
   fluids; remove the Ocean exclusion from `waterSideFaceQuads`. Generated
   Ocean remains level 8 and has no exposed sides beside equal neighbours.
   Edited or runtime partial Ocean uses the matching mask and exact sides.
   Existing differences in material, tint, and ice-cover policy remain.
5. Retain #2520's integer-ceiling convention for fluid top slice ownership.
   For exact surface `u`, slice `S`, and effective depth `D`, the vertical
   visibility window is `S - D <= surfaceCeilingZ u <= S`; screen-space
   culling uses the actual fractional placement. Side visibility and sort
   ordering must compose correctly with those tops. Equivalent geometry
   must agree within a chunk, across an ordinary loaded seam, and across
   the cylindrical U seam at all four camera facings. Use the production
   canonical neighbour lookup, including its unloaded-neighbour behavior.
6. Preserve existing ice elevations and modes. Ice renders at `icSurface`,
   not at the fluid ceiling. Where the ice base consumes a fluid height,
   use its documented integer ceiling: the base remains the maximum of
   terrain and that ceiling; drape remains base + 1, and basin ice retains
   its existing fill-level choice and 20-z thickness cap. Dry drape/basin
   behavior and whole-z ice results stay unchanged. Retain Lake/Ocean top
   suppression under existing ice cover, including partial fluid cells.
7. Preserve terrain slope rendering, the terrain-bed rule, zoom-map water
   classification, existing fluid tint values, and tinting policy. This is
   a rendering integration, with no new worldgen or fluid dynamics policy.
8. Add GPU-free coverage under the exact headless group
   `World.Render.FluidLevels`, using production geometry, visibility,
   lookup, and binding paths rather than test-local copies of their rules.
   Cover all levels and exact multiples; negative absolute surfaces; zero
   as a wet whole-z plane over lower terrain; fractional vertex positions;
   same-z mixed neighbours; full stacks with partial caps; multi-z drops;
   unequal left/right neighbours; enclosed equal-height cells; sort
   ordering; all facings; ordinary and U-seam parity; unloaded neighbours;
   and Ocean/Lake geometry parity. Include initial/late handle binding and
   cache invalidation, plus covered partial Lake/Ocean and dry drape/basin
   ice regressions. Test actual production slice/depth decisions on both
   sides of each boundary. For example, with `S = 2`, `D = 2`, exact units
   `u = -1, 0, 1, 16` pass the vertical window, while `u = -8, -9, 17`
   fail. Inspect vertex/coverage endpoints as well as counts; quad counts
   alone do not prove the combined rendered silhouette.
9. Supply a focused, reproducible offscreen capture driver and owner-review
   scene. Show levels 1..8 beside dry terrain, adjacent mixed levels,
   unequal left/right neighbours, an enclosed equal-height cell, full-z
   stacks with partial caps, multi-z drops, and River/Lake/Lava/partial
   Ocean variants. Include loaded seams and the ice regressions. Capture
   all four facings at representative day and night lighting. Use exact
   fixture/edit state from #2520; do not assume its legacy integer Lua
   queries provide an exact-unit setter. Capture the prerequisite-complete
   base and implementation with the same scene recipe. The owner must
   approve the integrated result before final review and merge.
10. Update repo-wide comments and documentation that describe current
    fluid rendering, including obsolete whole-z placement and two-z side
    rules. Preserve accurate historical evidence, migration explanations,
    and earlier delivery-phase descriptions. Do not disposition findings
    reports or change their status markers. Required documentation,
    reproducible capture evidence, and the recorded owner verdict are
    completion criteria of this same code PR, finished before final review
    and merge. Do not defer them to a later documentation landing.

## Acceptance

```bash
cabal build all
cabal build synarchy-test-headless
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "World.Render.SideFace"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "World.Render.FluidLevels"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "World.Render.PickSeam"'
cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "World.Slope.slopeBit"'
python3 tools/check_texture_paths.py
```

Expected: warning-clean build; each named group runs nonzero examples and
passes; requirement 8 is covered; existing terrain slope and seam behavior
remain green; every texture reference resolves.

```bash
rg -n '≢ Ocean' src/World/Render/SideDecoQuads.hs
```

Expected: no matches (ripgrep exit 1), backed by the behavioral Ocean parity
tests rather than source inspection alone.

This PR adds the focused capture driver used by this command:

```bash
python3 tools/fluid_levels_render_capture.py --port 9429 --size 1280x720 --out /tmp/issue-2529-captures
```

Follow `tools/offscreen_probe.py`'s boot pattern: use `--offscreen`, wait for
readiness, use a non-8008 console port, and stop only the driver's own
engine. Record the exact base/branch capture invocations, source revisions,
resource roots, fixture state, camera and lighting settings, and output
paths so both runs can be reproduced. Retain the scene driver, capture
manifest, screenshots, and recorded owner verdict with the implementation
PR. Expected: the complete scene matrix renders at exact eighth heights,
with correct combined silhouettes, independently terminated sides, no
seam-specific gaps or overlap, and preserved ice elevations. Screenshots
support a human decision; they are not a byte-equality gate. Headless
success alone does not complete visual acceptance.

## Out of scope

- Generated-river eighth-level progression (DFL-5); generated rivers still
  use whole-z planes at level 8 in this slice.
- Exact-unit public diagnostics, dump, or cursor fields (DFL-6).
- Save-format changes, new fluid dynamics, or changes to ice generation
  policy, ice modes, or ice elevations beyond the prerequisite conversion.
- Animated interpolation, waves, foam, refraction, or smoothing.
- Eighth-level depth on zoom-map pixels.
- New masks, mask edits, material recolours, or tint-policy changes;
  #2525 owns the approved assets.

## Related

- Epic #2514 (DFL-4), phase 3, critical path. Blocked by #2517 (DFL-1),
  #2520 (DFL-2), and #2525 (DFL-3). DFL-5 and DFL-6 are blocked by this
  issue.
- `docs/discrete_fluid_levels_design.md`: Exact surface vocabulary, Flat
  step presentation, Level masks and assets; D-1, D-2, D-3, D-4, D-7,
  D-10, D-12.
- `docs/hydrology_pipeline.md` section 6 for ice ownership;
  `docs/engine_contracts.md` section Tile-coordinate seam frame for lookup
  parity.

## Automated cross-agent issue review

Reviewed against `master@5b677136fdac` by GPT-6-Astra (`gpt-6-astra` at `high`).

**Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED**

Corrections and spec additions below amend the implementation spec. Supporting context is non-normative. Open decisions remain unresolved and must not be guessed.

### Corrections
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Requirement 5 conflates fluid height with ice height. World.Fluid.Ice.computeChunkIce creates drape ice at max(terrain, fluid) + 1 and basin ice up to 20 z above that base; World.Render.Quads renders icSurface. Substituting the fluid ceiling would collapse that existing geometry (src/World/Fluid/Ice.hs:73–92; src/World/Render/Quads.hs:311–331).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Limit requirement 9 to descriptions of current behavior. Preserve historical evidence, migration explanations, and descriptions of earlier delivery phases; their whole-z references remain accurate (docs/discrete_fluid_levels_design.md, §§Persistence and migration and DFL-1; CLAUDE.md, findings-status ownership).

### Spec additions / clarifications
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Verify the combined silhouette of the selected top mask and separate side geometry. The approved masks already contain side pixels, so those pixels must participate in requirement 3's no-overlap and exact-endpoint contract. Include unequal left/right neighbour heights and an equal-height enclosed cell; counting side quads alone is insufficient (docs/discrete_fluid_levels_design.md, §Level masks and assets; src/Engine/Graphics/Vulkan/ShaderCode.hs:249–312).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Include both initial world binding and late structural-texture rebinding in requirement 1, with verification that each level resolves to its intended handle. The integration route also includes World.Texture.Types and handleWorldSetTextureCommand, whose cache invalidation must be retained (scripts/world_manager.lua:11; scripts/world_view.lua:142; src/World/Thread/Command/Texture.hs).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Extend requirement 7 with negative absolute surfaces, zero as an exact whole-z wet plane, and partial surfaces on both sides of the effective-depth boundary. Pin slice ownership to the prerequisite's documented ceiling convention and test actual production visibility decisions (docs/discrete_fluid_levels_design.md, §Exact surface vocabulary; src/World/Render/Quads.hs:340).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Keep required documentation, reproducible capture evidence, and the recorded owner verdict within this implementation PR's completion criteria before final review and merge, following the supplied AGENTS.md publication-lane agreement.

### Supporting context
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Snapshot 5b677136fdacb75a604da796e066c50710c128b7 confirms integer top placement, whole-z side stacks, and the Ocean side exclusion; the requested fractional rendering is not already implemented (src/World/Render/TileQuads.hs; src/World/Render/SideDecoQuads.hs).
- **GPT-6-Astra:** The declared prerequisite split matches the tracked design: DFL-2 supplies exact state, DFL-3 supplies approved masks, and DFL-4 owns rendering integration. Their absence from this snapshot is not a blocker (docs/discrete_fluid_levels_design.md, §Delivery plan).

### Open decisions
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Should requirement 5 preserve icSurface and the existing drape/basin elevations, using the fluid ceiling only when deriving their base, or intentionally relocate covered ice to the fluid ceiling? These produce materially different geometry, and the latter exceeds a straightforward fluid-render conversion (src/World/Fluid/Ice.hs:73–92; issue requirement 5).

### Recommended disposition
- **GPT-6-Astra:** Clarify requirement 5 before readiness approval. Recommend preserving the existing ice elevations and adding covered partial Lake/Ocean plus dry drape/basin regression cases; if relocation is intentional, explicitly scope that behavior and its acceptance evidence (src/World/Fluid/Ice.hs; src/World/Render/Quads.hs).

### Reviewer summaries
- **GPT-6-Astra — CHANGES REQUESTED:** The rendering scope is viable with the declared prerequisites assumed landed. Requirement 5 needs an owner decision: placing ice at the fluid ceiling would replace the existing independently elevated ice surface.

## Automated cross-agent issue rereview

Reviewed against `master@c3a4cd1331ba` by Claude Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1` at `high`).

**Verdict: APPROVE**

Corrections and spec additions below amend the implementation spec. Supporting context is non-normative. Open decisions remain unresolved and must not be guessed.

### Corrections
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Background: the snapshot is now c3a4cd13, where #2525 has landed. The approved masks are assets/textures/facemap/isoface_level_1.png … isoface_level_8.png (docs/art/fluid_levels/README.md), generated by generateFluidLevelFaceMap in src/World/Slope/FaceMaps.hs:60-78; each mask's opaque side extends exactly 2*level rows below the fixed diamond footprint (line 75). Requirement 1's 'documented mask handle' refers to these files. #2517 and #2520 remain unlanded in this snapshot and stay assumed prerequisites.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Requirement 3 clarification (not a contradiction): every approved mask, like today's isoface.png, always carries its own top-slab side pixels regardless of neighbours; 'no exposed side' for equal or higher neighbours and 'no invented edge' for unloaded neighbours are satisfied by painter-order occlusion of those pixels by the front neighbour's top (the same mechanism whole-z terrain sides use today, see sort keys in src/World/Render/SideDecoQuads.hs:163-165), plus emitting NO separate side geometry in those cases. The exact-interval and no-duplicate rule therefore governs the separately emitted full-z/partial side segments together with the mask's 2*level side rows, evaluated after occlusion. Headless tests assert the separate-geometry endpoints, the selected level mask per cell, and absence of separate geometry for equal/higher/unloaded neighbours; the offscreen capture is the evidence for the post-occlusion silhouette.

### Spec additions / clarifications
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Requirement 1: add the eight level masks to every enumeration the existing entries use: the worldStructuralPaths preload list in scripts/startup_loader.lua:299+, worldView.ensureStructuralTextures and worldView.rebindStructural in scripts/world_view.lua:88-175, the string keys in parseTextureType (src/Engine/Scripting/Lua/Material.hs:19-37), the texture-type constructors in World.Texture.Types, the WorldTextures fields in World.Render.Textures.Types, and handleWorldSetTextureCommand, whose existing invalidation (bumpQuadCacheGen plus clearing wsZoomQuadCacheRef and wsBgQuadCacheRef, src/World/Thread/Command/Texture.hs:84-86) must run for each new key. Document the chosen world.setTexture key names alongside the mask file names in docs/art/fluid_levels/README.md or docs/asset_generation.md §Fluid level masks. Binding all eight files is required even though the generated level-8 pixels equal the flat face map (src/World/Slope/FaceMaps.hs:52-54).
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Requirement 9: the capture driver must author partial-level cells through a path #2520 actually delivers (its exact world-edits v2 snapshot replay, its fixture corpus loaded via engine.loadSave, or active-solver volume), and the capture manifest must name that path. The existing world.setFluidTile(page, gx, gy, kind) takes no height (src/Engine/Scripting/Lua/API/World/Edit.hs:422-446) and #2520's contract (docs/discrete_fluid_levels_design.md §DFL-2, §Out of scope line 208) promises no exact-unit Lua setter. If no #2520 path can author a specific level from the offscreen console, the PR may add a debug-scoped exact edit hook used only by the driver and headless tests, registered through the normal Lua registration audit, without changing any existing query's return arity; public exact diagnostics remain DFL-6 (#2535).
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Acceptance: add `cabal test synarchy-test-headless --test-options='--match "World.Slope.FaceMaps"'` and `python3 tools/fluid_level_masks.py --check-generated` (documented in docs/asset_generation.md:58-93) as gates for requirement 3's 'preserve the approved mask files'; both exist in the snapshot (test-headless/Spec.hs:1096) and must stay green with unchanged mask bytes.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Requirement 9 / tools: the capture driver is manual-only and GPU-dependent (offscreen Vulkan); do not add it to any CI selector or probe registry, and give it a tools/README.md entry. Follow tools/offscreen_probe.py (usage at line 93: --port, --size; screenshot helper at line 269) for boot, readiness, and screenshot capture.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Requirement 7 note: src/World/ZoomMap/Cache/Pixels.hs:77 has its own `fcType fc ≢ Ocean` branch for zoom-map water classification; it is intentionally outside requirement 4's Ocean side-exclusion removal (the acceptance grep is scoped to SideDecoQuads.hs) and must remain unchanged.

### Supporting context
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Prior open decision resolved: requirement 6 keeps ice at icSurface, base = max(terrain, fluid ceiling), drape = base + 1, basin = min(iceLevel, base + 20), matching src/World/Fluid/Ice.hs:40 (maxBasinThickness = 20) and :78-92; Lake/Ocean top suppression under ice is at src/World/Render/Quads.hs:352-358.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Requirement 8's window example checks out under a ceiling convention: with S=2, D=2, ceil(u/8) for u = -1, 0, 1, 16 gives 0, 0, 1, 2 (inside [0,2]); for u = -8, -9, 17 gives -1, -1, 3 (outside). This mirrors the existing integer rejection `fcSurface fc > zSlice ∨ fcSurface fc < zSlice - effectiveDepth` at src/World/Render/Quads.hs:341 and the side-quad window at src/World/Render/SideDecoQuads.hs:70-71.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Ocean exclusion and whole-z two-z side rule confirmed present: src/World/Render/SideDecoQuads.hs:48 (`fcType fc ≢ Ocean`) and :56-69 (draw only for gaps ≥ 2, one quad per z). Requirement 4 and the `rg -n '≢ Ocean'` acceptance target this file only.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** All named acceptance groups exist in test-headless/Spec.hs: World.Render.PickSeam (1037), World.Render.SideFace (1094), World.Slope.slopeBit (1095), World.Slope.FaceMaps (1096). `World.Render.FluidLevels` is new and does not substring-collide with any existing describe name. tools/check_texture_paths.py and tools/offscreen_probe.py exist.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Prerequisite status in snapshot: #2525 landed (assets, generator, docs/art/fluid_levels/README.md owner approval 2026-09-10); #2517 not landed (World.Render.WaterSlope still imported and used at src/World/Render/Quads.hs:41,376,385); #2520 not landed (FluidCell.fcSurface ∷ Int; no surfaceCeilingZ/topFillLevel anywhere under src/). Per dependency policy these are assumed contracts; the design doc §Delivery plan DFL-4 scope matches this issue.
- **Claude Fable 5.1:** Design doc processing status marks DFL-5 as #2533 and DFL-6 as #2535; this issue's out-of-scope list correctly defers generated-river progression and exact diagnostics to them, so no duplicate is visible from the dossier or the tracked design.

### Reviewer summaries
- **Claude Fable 5.1 — APPROVE:** The revision resolves the prior changes-requested review: requirement 6 now preserves icSurface, drape base+1, and the 20-z basin cap exactly as src/World/Fluid/Ice.hs:40,78-92 and src/World/Render/Quads.hs:318-334 implement them, so the ice open decision is closed; requirements 1, 3, 8, and 10 absorb the earlier spec additions (initial plus late rebinding with cache invalidation, combined mask-plus-side silhouette with unequal neighbours and enclosed cells, negative/zero/window-boundary coverage, docs and owner verdict inside the code PR). Against snapshot c3a4cd13, #2525 has landed (eight isoface_level_N.png masks, World.Slope.FaceMaps generator, owner approval record) while #2517 and #2520 have not (waterSlopeAt still imported at src/World/Render/Quads.hs:41; fcSurface is Int at src/World/Fluid/Types.hs:33; no topFillLevel); both are declared prerequisites and are assumed. The spec is consistent, testable, and one-PR sized. Amendments below pin how the mask's built-in side pixels interact with the no-overlap contract, how the capture driver may author partial cells given that #2520 promises no exact Lua setter, and add the #2525 preservation gates to acceptance.
